messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — PD-4512 — service=hosted-inference — symptom=5xx spike (502/503) in us-west-2, current rate 18% errors over 2m window. Escalation policy=standard-oncall.
pagerduty: Notification sent to primary on-call @Alice M. — no ACK after 90s, auto-escalating to secondary @Ben K.
Alice M.: I'm on mobile, getting dinged. Can someone paste the quick metrics?
Ben K.: ack — looking now. grabbing logs and checking recent deploys.
Dave R.: seeing repeated upstream 502 from model-proxy, connection reset between proxy and GPU pool (TLS handshake errors). Correlates with spike start +3m after a leader election.
Emma L.: Support FYI — we already have two customers reporting elevated 5xx on embeddings endpoint. Ticket numbers in Zendesk: 98712, 98718.
Ben K.: running quick health checks:
```
curl -sSf https://hosted-api.us-west-2.redwood.ai/health | jq .
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=hosted-api -o wide
```
Ben K.: pod list shows 3/5 pods Ready for model-proxy, rest are CrashLoopBackoff with logs: `failed to init kv cache: permission denied` — suspect a config/secret rotated.
Carla S.: manager notified by PD due to missed primary ack window. Joining thread now. How widespread is customer impact?
Emma L.: approx 15% of requests failing for embeddings and generation in us-west-2, latency for successful requests up ~300ms. No data exfiltration reported. Customers on Dedicated regions unaffected so far.
ops-oncall: Attempting to roll back the last config push to model-proxy (deployed ~17:12 UTC). If rollback fails, we'll restart replicas to force reinit.
Ben K.: trying config inspect: secret name mismatch in deployment spec — looks like a new secret name `kv-cache-key-v2` is referenced but not present in namespace. That explains the permission denied errors.
Dave R.: confirming — K8s events show `FailedMount` for secret volume. PD escalation to manager is appropriate.
Carla S.: Good catch. Ben, can you patch the deployment to fallback to previous secret name while we validate the new one? If yes, do it and report back.
Ben K.: patching now. Command: `kubectl -n inference set env deployment/model-proxy KV_SECRET=kv-cache-key-v1 && kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-proxy`
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-4512 acknowledged by Ben K. at 3416789120
Ben K.: rollout started. pods coming up. Monitor shows error rate dropping from 18% -> 6% within 60s.
Dave R.: cache init successful on restarted pods. No more TLS handshake errors in logs.
Emma L.: notifying affected customers that we're mitigating; will open followups for those two Zendesk tickets.
Carla S.: thumbs — Ben, please keep it in your court for the next hour, we'll do a short postmortem and fix the secret rotation automation. Anyone have objections to closing the PD incident once errors <1% for 10m?
Alice M.: no objections, thanks for picking this up — I was on a delayed commute and missed the first page.
Ben K.: agreed. I'll hold and watch. Adding a watch command: `kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-proxy --tail=200 -f`
ops-oncall: I'll also update runbook to include a check for secret name validation step pre-deploy.
Carla S.: please also include a blameless note: rotation script introduced new secret name without namespace creation. Prioritize fix in deploy pipeline.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Manager escalation cleared — incident now owned by secondary (Ben K.).
Ben K.: error rate stabilized at ~0.4% over last 6m. Starting post-incident notes and timeline. Will follow up with a short RFC for secrets rollout.
Emma L.: Support will send a customer update summarizing impact & mitigation.
Dave R.: recommend a rollback-protect check in CI that verifies secret exists in target namespace. I'll draft a quick PR.
Carla S.: thanks team. I'll close the monitoring loop and hand this back to product/security to ensure secret management changes. Ben, please close PD when you see sustained <1% for 10m.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident PD-4512 resolved by Ben K. — closed at 3416790012.
Ben K.: closing PD now. Leaving a short incident thread for postmortem writeup. :thumbsup:
